derived_from: src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:343 MCPAutoLoaderTool.run -- reads only `operation`, `tool_name`, `tool_arguments`; raises ValueError for any other operation, None included.
src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:311 _run_with_cleanup -- no except clause, so a failure leaves run() as an exception rather than a value. That is why no error branch is declared.
src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:352 the discover branch -- sets discovered_count, tools and tool_details unconditionally.
src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:365 the generate_configs branch -- sets configs and count unconditionally.
src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:289 _make_mcp_request -- returns result.model_dump(mode='json') for the http transport.
src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py:1082 generate_proxy_tool_configs -- the eight keys it always sets and the nine it sets conditionally.

mcp.types.CallToolResult / mcp.types.Tool, introspected from the installed SDK: CallToolResult requires only `content` and model_dump emits meta/content/structuredContent/isError; Tool requires name and inputSchema and model_dump emits seven more as null.
how: Payloads were written from the branches above, not from a docstring. The three operations share no required key, so a real return matches exactly one branch; the mixed payload below is the negative control for that exclusivity.
the_trap: The old declaration was the placeholder {"type":"object","description":"Output of the tool execution.","properties":{}} for six of the seven, which accepts every payload here, reachable or not, and so can never fail. The input side was worse than vacuous: `parameter` had no properties at all, so the generated SDK wrapper hard-coded "arguments": {} and documented "No parameters" -- it could not make a successful call, because run() needs `operation`. test_examples was [{}], which `tu info` prints as the usage example and `tu test` executes.
invariant: A tool's test_examples must validate against its own `parameter` schema. [{}] does not, once `operation` is required -- that one rule is what makes the old example impossible to ship again.
note_on_carbon_a: mcp_auto_loader_carbon_a has no committed wrapper. build_tools.py only writes wrappers for tools that load, and these seven need a *_MCP_SERVER_HOST to load, so the six that do have one were generated by someone whose environment had that variable set. None was invented here.

discover_empty.why: A server that lists nothing. discovered_count is len(tool_details), so zero.

discover_two.why: Two tools as list_tools().model_dump(mode='json') renders them: name and inputSchema set, the other seven null.

generate_configs_empty.why: selected_tools filtered everything out, or the server listed nothing. count == len(configs).

generate_configs_one.why: One proxy config carrying only the eight keys generate_proxy_tool_configs always sets.

generate_configs_one_full.why: The same config once the loader sets strict_tool_contracts, normalize_mcp_result and friends, and the server published an outputSchema and annotations.

call_tool_ok.why: CallToolResult.model_dump(mode='json') for a successful call: all four keys present, isError false.

call_tool_server_reported_error.why: The server reported a tool-level failure. The call itself succeeded, so this arrives as a value on this branch, not as an exception.

call_tool_structured.why: A server that publishes an outputSchema also fills structuredContent.

call_tool_websocket_shape.why: The websocket branch of _make_mcp_request hands back the raw JSON-RPC result, where isError may simply be absent. This is why only `content` is required.

empty_object.why: What the old test_examples asked for and what the old wrapper always sent. No branch of run() can produce it.

discover_without_tool_details.why: The discover branch sets all three keys in one dict literal; two of three is not a state it can be in.

discover_descriptor_missing_input_schema.why: inputSchema is required on mcp.types.Tool, so the SDK cannot hand back a descriptor without it.

generate_configs_without_count.why: The generate_configs branch returns both keys in one dict literal.

generate_configs_config_missing_target.why: target_tool_name is set unconditionally on every config.

call_tool_without_content.why: content is the one field mcp.types.CallToolResult requires.

discover_and_generate_configs_at_once.why: Exclusivity control: run() takes one branch per call, so no return carries both shapes. A oneOf that matched this would not be discriminating.

a_list.why: Every branch is an object; no branch returns an array.
